userStories.title: Mark every session-sandbox wrapped command
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make every command wrapped by the session launcher advertise NAX_SANDBOXED=1, expose its constant publicly, and teach nax-agent's confined-test helper to recognize it.

**Motivation** — When a native agent runs `bun run test` through nax's own session sandbox, the variable is absent, so tests that `skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())` because they launch a real srt backend run anyway and fail (`sandbox wrap failed: EPERM: operation not permitted, listen` on the srt-mux socket; `mkdir /tmp/nax` denied).

**Approach** — Apply these verbatim Design targets:
- `tmpEnvPrefix(tmpDir)` / the prefix logic in `runWrapped` (`launcher.ts`).
  - Baseline: prefix is `export TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; ` when `env.tmpDir` is defined, and nothing otherwise.
  - Target: every wrapped command is prefixed. With `env.tmpDir` defined: `export NAX_SANDBOXED=1 TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; `. With it undefined: `export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; `. `runUnwrapped` is unchanged and adds no marker: an unwrapped command is not sandboxed. `executed` stays `logicalArgv(req)`. The comment above the prefix in `runWrapped` (the one explaining why TMPDIR rides the shell command) is updated to say the prefix now always carries `NAX_SANDBOXED=1`.
- New constant `SANDBOXED_ENV = "NAX_SANDBOXED"`, declared in `launcher.ts`, re-exported from `src/sandbox/index.ts` and from the package root `src/index.ts` so a consumer (a test helper, or a downstream project's tests) can read the marker by name.
- `isConfinedTestRun()` in `packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/confined.ts` and its sanctioned copy in `packages/nax/test/helpers/confined.ts`.
  - Baseline: `return process.env[CONFINED_TEST_ENV] === "1";`
  - Target: true when `process.env.NAX_TEST_CONFINED === "1"` **or** `process.env.NAX_SANDBOXED === "1"`; any other value of either reads as not confined. Each copy exports `SANDBOXED_ENV` alongside `CONFINED_TEST_ENV`. The nax-agent copy imports `SANDBOXED_ENV` from `#src/sandbox/index`; the nax copy declares the literal (the sanctioned-copy pattern the file already uses for `CONFINED_TEST_ENV`).

The helper design names both copies to document the seam; this story changes only the nax-agent copy. The nax copy is US-002. srt replaces the child environment wholesale, which is why the TMPDIR override rides the shell command rather than an env overlay. Preserve shell quoting and all logical command/audit identity. The marker variable is already set in the parent environment: irrelevant to wrapped runs, since srt replaces the child env and the prefix sets it. Unwrapped runs inherit the parent env unchanged, as today; no new inheritance test is required.

Implementation includes the following compatibility updates within packages/nax-agent: extend test/helpers/index.ts with SANDBOXED_ENV; update the three exact wrapped command assertions in test/unit/sandbox/launcher.test.ts (normal shell, denial shell, quoted argv); update the combined export in test/unit/sandbox/launcher-session-tmp.test.ts; update audit.sandbox.argv in test/unit/tools/bash-sandbox.test.ts and both audit.sandbox.argv and seen[0].argv in test/unit/tools/run-command-exec-sandbox.test.ts. Keep executed, stdout and hint-line assertions unchanged. In test/unit/scripts/confined-run.test.ts, helper cases must save, clear and restore both markers, and runFixture must delete both markers from copied process.env before setting the runner marker; preserve every existing outcome. In test/fixtures/confined/writes-literal-tmp.fixture.ts and writes-tmpdir.fixture.ts, change only the guard to use process.env[CONFINED_TEST_ENV] === "1" directly instead of isConfinedTestRun(), retaining runner-only fixture semantics and the intentional literal-/tmp failure. Regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt with bun run api:update so SANDBOXED_ENV appears under both . and ./internal (internal.ts already re-exports the sandbox barrel).

**Scope** — In: launcher prefix and comments, constant exports, nax-agent helper/barrel, package-local exact-command assertions, fixture guard/env-isolation adjustments, and public API snapshot. Out: US-002's nax helper and child-process proof; US-003's gate resolver. Do not mark unwrapped runs, change the confined runner, change ACP shell commands, or rewrite/stub/weaken sandbox-dependent skipIf consumers.

**Interface** — Spec identifiers and unchanged call shapes: `tmpEnvPrefix(tmpDir)`, `runWrapped(req, backend, policy, env)`, `runUnwrapped`, `createCommandLauncher`, `isConfinedTestRun()`, `SANDBOXED_ENV = "NAX_SANDBOXED"`; no launcher request/result signature change. Existing TypeScript helper signature remains `export function isConfinedTestRun(): boolean`.

**Verification** — Use strict three-session-tdd for the session-sandbox execution path: first prepare failing regressions and mechanical test/fixture updates without source changes, then implement without editing tests, then verify. Reuse makeFakeSandboxBackend and _launcherDeps, not a real nested srt launch; restore both process.env markers in all mutating cases. Demonstrate new behavior fails against old code. No new files are required.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createCommandLauncher in the available state with a fake enforcing backend and no tmpDir, running the shell spec echo hi, passes backend.wrap the command export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; echo hi.

[unit] createCommandLauncher in the available state with tmpDir set to <t>, running the shell spec echo hi, passes backend.wrap the command export NAX_SANDBOXED=1 TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; echo hi.

[unit] createCommandLauncher in the available state with no tmpDir, running the argv spec ["echo", "a b"], passes backend.wrap the command export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; 'echo' 'a b' and returns stdout a b after trimming.
[unit] createCommandLauncher in the available state with a fake backend that executes the wrapped command, running the shell spec printenv NAX_SANDBOXED, returns stdout 1 after trimming.

[unit] createCommandLauncher in the disabled state, with NAX_SANDBOXED deleted from process.env for the test and restored afterwards, running the shell spec printenv NAX_SANDBOXED, returns empty stdout after trimming and a result whose sandbox.wrapped is false.

[unit] createCommandLauncher in the unavailable state, with NAX_SANDBOXED deleted from process.env for the test and restored afterwards, running the shell spec printenv NAX_SANDBOXED, returns empty stdout after trimming and a result whose sandbox.wrapped is false.
[unit] (regression pin) For the shell spec echo hi, the executed field of the LaunchResult from the available state equals the executed field the same request yields from the disabled state.
[unit] SANDBOXED_ENV imported from the nax-agent package root (src/index.ts) equals the string NAX_SANDBOXED.
[unit] SANDBOXED_ENV imported from src/sandbox/index.ts is the same value as the one imported from the package root.
[unit] The nax-agent test helper isConfinedTestRun() returns true when NAX_SANDBOXED is "1" and NAX_TEST_CONFINED is unset.
[unit] (regression pin) The nax-agent test helper isConfinedTestRun() returns true when NAX_TEST_CONFINED is "1" and NAX_SANDBOXED is unset.
[unit] (regression pin) The nax-agent test helper isConfinedTestRun() returns false when both NAX_SANDBOXED and NAX_TEST_CONFINED are unset.
[unit] (regression pin) The nax-agent test helper isConfinedTestRun() returns false when NAX_SANDBOXED is "true" and NAX_TEST_CONFINED is unset.

routing.reasoning: The implementation is a localized prefix and exact-value helper change using existing launch/export patterns; the additional files are mechanical API, fixture and expectation updates, not new abstractions. Retain strict three-session-tdd under the session-sandbox security override, not because the advisory marker is itself a security boundary.

suggestedCriteria: When session-temp directory creation fails for an available launcher, backend.wrap still receives export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; echo hi without any TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP assignment for the request echo hi.
When NAX_TEST_CONFINED is "1" and NAX_SANDBOXED is "0", the nax-agent isConfinedTestRun() returns true.
When only NAX_SANDBOXED=1 is set and NAX_TEST_CONFINED is absent, explicitly running either confined fixture with bun test exits 0 with stderr containing 1 skip.

modifiedFiles.reason: three tests pin the wrapped command, which now starts with export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; whether or not a session temp dir is in force. (1) "available: wraps, runs the wrapper argv, records wrapped" asserts r.sandbox equals { backend: "srt", wrapped: true, argv: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"] }; the argv becomes ["/bin/sh", "-c", "export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; echo hi"]. (2) "a likely denial appends the hint line" asserts the argv ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo 'x: Operation not permitted' >&2; exit 1"]; it becomes ["/bin/sh", "-c", "export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; echo 'x: Operation not permitted' >&2; exit 1"]. (3) "available: an argv spec is quoted into one shell command" asserts backend.calls[0]?.command is exactly the quoted argv; the expected command gains the same leading export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; . In all three, executed, stdout and the hint line are unchanged.

the assertion at line 106 expects the wrapped command export TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; echo hi; the marker joins the same export, so the expected command becomes export NAX_SANDBOXED=1 TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; echo hi.

line 69 asserts audit.sandbox equals { backend: "srt", wrapped: true, argv: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"] }; the wrapped argv now carries the marker prefix, so it becomes ["/bin/sh", "-c", "export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; echo hi"]. audit.executed (the logical argv) is unchanged.

lines 57-63 assert audit.sandbox.argv and the spawned seen[0].argv equal ["/bin/sh", "-c", "'bun' '--version'"]; both become ["/bin/sh", "-c", "export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; 'bun' '--version'"]. The invariant (the argv the backend built is the argv spawned) is unchanged.

two places read the confined marker from an environment that, inside a sandboxed session, now also carries NAX_SANDBOXED=1. (1) The isConfinedTestRun describe block saves and restores only NAX_TEST_CONFINED; it must also save, clear and restore NAX_SANDBOXED. (2) runFixture in the "confined fixtures" describe block copies process.env and deletes only NAX_TEST_CONFINED; it must also delete NAX_SANDBOXED, or the "without the confined marker" runs read as confined. Every asserted outcome is unchanged.

the fixture runs only under the confined runner via skipIf(!isConfinedTestRun()), and is built to FAIL there (it writes a literal /tmp path). Once isConfinedTestRun() also reads NAX_SANDBOXED, a gate that runs this path explicitly inside a sandboxed session would run it and record the designed failure. Its guard must read the runner's marker directly (process.env.NAX_TEST_CONFINED equal to "1", via CONFINED_TEST_ENV) instead of isConfinedTestRun(); its behaviour under the runner is unchanged.

same guard as writes-literal-tmp.fixture.ts: skipIf(!isConfinedTestRun()) must read the runner's marker directly (CONFINED_TEST_ENV equal to "1"), so the fixture keeps meaning running under the confined runner and is not run by a sandboxed session; its behaviour under the runner is unchanged.
isConfinedTestRun() gains the NAX_SANDBOXED reading and the file exports SANDBOXED_ENV (imported from #src/sandbox/index), per the Design target.
the barrel re-exports CONFINED_TEST_ENV and isConfinedTestRun from ./confined; it also re-exports SANDBOXED_ENV.

the committed public-API snapshot gains SANDBOXED_ENV under both the . and ./internal entry points (internal.ts re-exports the sandbox barrel); regenerate it with bun run api:update so check:api passes.

userStories.title: Recognize the sandbox marker in nax's confined-test helper
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Teach nax's sanctioned confined-test helper copy to recognize the session sandbox marker and prove an unchanged sandbox-dependent suite skips in a marked child process.

**Motivation** — Every workflow run whose story tests execute inside the session sandbox can repeat that.

**Approach** — Apply the following verbatim Design target to the nax copy only; US-001 owns the nax-agent copy and package export:
- `isConfinedTestRun()` in `packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/confined.ts` and its sanctioned copy in `packages/nax/test/helpers/confined.ts`.
  - Baseline: `return process.env[CONFINED_TEST_ENV] === "1";`
  - Target: true when `process.env.NAX_TEST_CONFINED === "1"` **or** `process.env.NAX_SANDBOXED === "1"`; any other value of either reads as not confined. Each copy exports `SANDBOXED_ENV` alongside `CONFINED_TEST_ENV`. The nax-agent copy imports `SANDBOXED_ENV` from `#src/sandbox/index`; the nax copy declares the literal (the sanctioned-copy pattern the file already uses for `CONFINED_TEST_ENV`).

The sanctioned copy of `isConfinedTestRun()` in `packages/nax/test/helpers/confined.ts` reads `NAX_SANDBOXED` as well as `NAX_TEST_CONFINED`, and exports `SANDBOXED_ENV`, whose value matches the one `@nathapp/nax-agent` exports. Preserve the sanctioned-copy pattern, update the helper's runner-only commentary, and re-export SANDBOXED_ENV through test/helpers/index.ts. In test/unit/helpers/confined.test.ts, save, clear and restore both environment markers so false cases remain meaningful inside sandboxed sessions; retain existing runner-marker outcomes and test the public-constant agreement via @test/helpers and @nathapp/nax-agent.

Create test/integration/confined/sandbox-marker.test.ts. Spawn `bun test test/unit/agents/coding-tool-support-session-tmp.test.ts` from packages/nax with NAX_SANDBOXED=1 and NAX_TEST_CONFINED removed from a copied child environment; assert exit 0 and stderr containing 1 skip, where bun test writes its summary. Use a real child process, safely capture/drain its streams and do not simulate the summary. The target suite already uses skipIf(isConfinedTestRun()), so leave it unchanged. Also update test/integration/permissions/bash-deny-suite.test.ts's final backend.calls[0]?.command expectation to `export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; ` followed by the original command; retain the two preceding expectations that the policy/ask and command shadow see unprefixed bytes and update the misleading identical-backend-bytes comment.

**Scope** — In: nax's helper and barrel, env-isolated helper regressions, public constant agreement, exact backend transport expectation, and the new child-process integration proof. Out: US-001's launcher, nax-agent helper and API snapshot; US-003's gate scheduling. US-002 only: the two tests named in #2601, `test/unit/agents/coding-tool-support-command-shadow.test.ts` and `test/unit/agents/coding-tool-support-session-tmp.test.ts`, are not modified; they already `skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())` and start skipping once the helper reads the marker. No test that calls `skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())` is rewritten, stubbed or weakened to make it pass inside a sandbox. The marker is advisory, not an authorization check or external-sandbox detector.

**Interface** — Preserve `isConfinedTestRun()` and `CONFINED_TEST_ENV`; add `SANDBOXED_ENV = "NAX_SANDBOXED"` to the helper/barrel exports. Existing TypeScript helper signature remains `export function isConfinedTestRun(): boolean`. US-001 → US-002: `SANDBOXED_ENV` exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent` is the name the nax helper copy must agree with (US-002 AC 4 pins the agreement).

**Verification** — Use tdd-simple: write the failing marker/helper and real-child regressions first, then implement the helper change. Restore both environment values even after failures. Run explicit test paths; do not launch a new real nested srt backend or alter the target suite to manufacture a skip.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] isConfinedTestRun() from @test/helpers returns true when NAX_SANDBOXED is "1" and NAX_TEST_CONFINED is unset.
[unit] (regression pin) isConfinedTestRun() from @test/helpers returns false when both NAX_SANDBOXED and NAX_TEST_CONFINED are unset.
[unit] (regression pin) isConfinedTestRun() from @test/helpers returns false when NAX_SANDBOXED is "0" and NAX_TEST_CONFINED is unset.
[unit] SANDBOXED_ENV exported by @test/helpers equals SANDBOXED_ENV exported by @nathapp/nax-agent.

[integration] test/integration/confined/sandbox-marker.test.ts spawns bun test test/unit/agents/coding-tool-support-session-tmp.test.ts from packages/nax with NAX_SANDBOXED=1 set and NAX_TEST_CONFINED removed in the child environment; the child exits 0 and its stderr (where bun test writes its summary) contains 1 skip.

routing.reasoning: A standard helper/barrel change with exact environment semantics, an existing byte-expectation adjustment and one bounded child-process proof. It consumes an advisory marker without changing session lifecycle or permission/access-control decisions.

suggestedCriteria: When NAX_TEST_CONFINED is "1" and NAX_SANDBOXED is unset, isConfinedTestRun() from @test/helpers returns true.
When NAX_TEST_CONFINED is unset and NAX_SANDBOXED is "true", isConfinedTestRun() from @test/helpers returns false.

modifiedFiles.reason: the isConfinedTestRun describe block saves and restores only NAX_TEST_CONFINED, and its "returns false" tests would read true inside a sandboxed session. It must also save, clear and restore NAX_SANDBOXED; the asserted outcomes are unchanged.
isConfinedTestRun() gains the NAX_SANDBOXED reading and the file exports SANDBOXED_ENV, per the Design target.
the barrel re-exports the confined helpers from ./confined; it also re-exports SANDBOXED_ENV.

line 641 asserts backend.calls[0]?.command is exactly the agent's command ("the backend's wrap saw the identical bytes"); the launcher now prefixes every wrapped command, so the expected value becomes export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; followed by command. The invariant that the policy check and the shadow see the unprefixed bytes (the two assertions above it) is unchanged.

userStories.title: Run root-configured repo gates once per gate key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make root quality.commands take precedence per gate key while retaining overlay-only gates and existing deduplication for remaining overlay runs.

**Motivation** — In a monorepo whose root commands fan out across the workspace (`bun run --filter '*' test`, `turbo run test`), the overlay's package-local command never matches, so the package's suite runs twice per gate round.

**Approach** — Apply these verbatim Design targets:
- The overlay loop in `resolveGateCommands(repoRoot, packageDirs)` (`quality.ts`). Signature unchanged.
  - Baseline: for each package dir and each `GATE_ORDER` key the overlay configures, schedule `<gate>@<pkg>` unless the run `(cwd, command, setup)` is already scheduled.
  - Target: same loop, plus one rule evaluated first: when the root configures that gate key (`isConfigured(rootCommands[gate])`), the overlay's command for that key is skipped. "Configured" uses the existing `isConfigured` (a blank string or an array of blanks is not configured). The existing run-identity dedupe stays for the keys that do reach it. The header comment's F2 paragraph is updated to state the root-wins rule.

Order of evaluation in `resolveGateCommands`, per overlay gate key: (1) not set in the overlay → skip; (2) root configures the key → skip; (3) run identity already scheduled → skip; (4) schedule `<gate>@<pkg>`. Root gates are scheduled first, in `GATE_ORDER`, exactly as today.

Keep root layered loadConfig resolution and package-own loadPackageOverride resolution, rather than using the deep-merged story config. Root precedence applies regardless of command text, cwd or differing setup. Root nonblank arrays configure a key just as nonblank strings do. e2eSetup is setup metadata, not a gate key: if root provides only e2eSetup, an overlay e2e still schedules and inherits that root setup unless explicitly overridden. Keep root per-key identity (two root keys sharing command bytes still yield two root gates), overlay run identity (cwd, command, setup), package input ordering, GATE_ORDER ordering and empty package-dir filtering. Update the resolver's identity commentary as well as the header so it no longer promises to retain a same-key overlay e2e with a different setup when root already configures e2e.

Update test/unit/finish/gates-quality.test.ts: the root-four-gates plus test overlay case now expects ["build", "typecheck", "lint", "test"]; the ordering case now expects ["build", "typecheck", "test", "lint@pkg-b", "lint@pkg-a"]. Preserve their ordering/no-backfill invariants. In test/unit/finish/gates-quality-e2e.test.ts, the existing different-e2eSetup case now expects only root e2e with setup docker compose up -d. Add the remaining concrete root/fallback/blank/array cases using existing configWithCommands helpers and restored _qualityGateDeps. Extend test/unit/workflow/repo-gates.test.ts to run the real resolveGateCommands with stubbed _qualityGateDeps.loadConfig and loadPackageOverride and capture _featureDeps.runQualityGates commands. Restore both dependency seams. Do not stub the resolver's return for this integration assertion.

The resolver change reaches the workflow through the existing `runRepoGates` → `_featureDeps.resolveGateCommands` call (US-003 AC 9). Finish's existing gates-loop call also inherits the rule unchanged. A loadPackageOverride exception still propagates from resolveGateCommands; no new test for that unchanged failure is required.

**Scope** — In: shared gate resolver's root-wins condition and comments, resolver/e2e expectation updates, and a workflow consumer proof. Out: US-001's sandbox launcher and US-002's confined helper. `nax gates run` behaviour is unchanged (it already resolves root gates only). Story-level command resolution (`loadConfigForWorkdir`, `testScoped`, the per-story verify) is unchanged: overlays still set each story's commands. Do not remove overlay commands or rewrite workflow/finish callers. Project migration and release-note updates are not implementation stories.

**Interface** — Spec call shape `resolveGateCommands(repoRoot, packageDirs)` remains unchanged. Existing TypeScript signature remains `export async function resolveGateCommands(repoRoot: string, packageDirs: string[]): Promise<GateCommand[]>`. `GateCommand` retains name, command, cwd and optional setup; root names remain <gate> and fallback overlay names remain <gate>@<pkg>.

**Verification** — Use tdd-simple: show the same-key root/overlay regressions fail on the old resolver, then add the precedence check. Keep all existing overlay-only F2, cross-key run-dedupe, root per-key identity and e2e setup-inheritance behavior covered; no new files are required.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With root quality.commands { test: "root test" } and an apps/web overlay { test: "bun test apps/web" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["apps/web"]) returns exactly [{ name: "test", command: "root test", cwd: "/repo" }].

[unit] With root commands { build: "root build", typecheck: "root typecheck", lint: "root lint", test: "root test" } and an apps/web overlay { test: "bun test apps/web" }, the returned gate names are ["build", "typecheck", "lint", "test"].

[unit] With root commands { test: "root test" } and a pkg overlay { build: "bun run build" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns [{ name: "test", command: "root test", cwd: "/repo" }, { name: "build@pkg", command: "bun run build", cwd: "/repo/pkg" }].

[unit] With no root quality.commands and an apps/web overlay { test: "bun test apps/web" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["apps/web"]) returns [{ name: "test@apps/web", command: "bun test apps/web", cwd: "/repo/apps/web" }].

[unit] With root commands { lint: "   " } and a pkg overlay { lint: "biome lint" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns [{ name: "lint@pkg", command: "biome lint", cwd: "/repo/pkg" }], because a blank root command does not configure the key.

[unit] With root commands { test: "root test" } and overlays for pkg-b and pkg-a each { test: "pkg test", lint: "pkg lint" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg-b", "pkg-a"]) returns gate names ["test", "lint@pkg-b", "lint@pkg-a"].

[unit] With root commands { e2e: "bunx playwright test", e2eSetup: "docker compose up -d" } and a . overlay { e2e: "bunx playwright test", e2eSetup: "docker compose -f other.yml up -d" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["."]) returns only the root e2e gate, with setup docker compose up -d.

[unit] With root commands { e2eSetup: "root setup" } (no root e2e) and a pkg overlay { e2e: "journey" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns [{ name: "e2e@pkg", command: "journey", cwd: "/repo/pkg", setup: "root setup" }].

[unit] Given fc.packageDirs ["packages/api"], _featureDeps.resolveGateCommands bound to the real resolveGateCommands, _qualityGateDeps.loadConfig returning a NaxConfig whose quality.commands is { test: "root test" }, _qualityGateDeps.loadPackageOverride returning a package override whose quality.commands is { test: "api test" }, and _featureDeps.runQualityGates stubbed to capture commands, workflow runRepoGates(fc) calls runQualityGates with commands whose names are exactly ["test"].

[unit] With root commands { lint: ["biome lint", "tsc --noEmit"] } and a pkg overlay { lint: "pkg lint" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns only the root lint gate, because a non-blank array configures the key.

routing.reasoning: One localized resolver condition with three existing test modules and existing dependency seams; ordering, overlay-only fallback and e2e setup rules are already implemented and must be preserved. No new abstraction or access-control logic is introduced.

suggestedCriteria: With root commands { lint: ["  ", ""] } and a pkg overlay { lint: "biome lint" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns exactly [{ name: "lint@pkg", command: "biome lint", cwd: "/repo/pkg" }].

With root commands {} and a pkg overlay { build: "bun run tsc", typecheck: "bun run tsc" }, resolveGateCommands("/repo", ["pkg"]) returns exactly [{ name: "build@pkg", command: "bun run tsc", cwd: "/repo/pkg" }].
With root commands { build: "tsc --noEmit", typecheck: "tsc --noEmit" } and no overlays, resolveGateCommands("/repo", []) returns gate names ["build", "typecheck"].

modifiedFiles.reason: two tests expect an overlay gate for a key the root also configures. (1) "a package overlay that sets only one gate does not fan out the root's other gates for that package" expects ["build", "typecheck", "lint", "test", "test@apps/web"]; the root configures test, so the expected names become ["build", "typecheck", "lint", "test"]. (2) "orders root gates by GATE_ORDER, then each package's gates by GATE_ORDER, packages in order given" expects build@pkg-b and build@pkg-a; the root configures build, so the expected names become ["build", "typecheck", "test", "lint@pkg-b", "lint@pkg-a"]. The ordering invariant (root gates first, then each package in the order given) still holds.

the test "AC-6: same e2e command and cwd but different e2eSetup keeps both gates" expects both e2e and e2e@.; the root configures e2e, so the overlay's e2e is skipped and the expected result is the root e2e gate alone, with setup docker compose up -d.

analysis:
This enhancement closes #2601 and #2603; it is not greenfield. Codebase-memory MCP was unavailable, so the investigation used direct reads and text search. The checked source matches the spec's baseline. Architecture guidance was read at docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:11 (dependency injection/conventions), :29 (testing/async standards), :95 (sandbox and trust-boundary ownership), and :149 (package dependency direction). Exactly three stories retain the binding IDs, package workdirs and dependencies: US-001 in packages/nax-agent; US-002 in packages/nax depending on US-001; independent US-003 in packages/nax. No new abstraction, dependency, schema, configuration flag or package is needed.

US-001 — launcher and library contract. packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/launcher.ts:65 defines logicalArgv; :75 defines tmpEnvPrefix with the existing single-quote escaping; :108 defines runUnwrapped; :122 defines runWrapped; :128 converts shell/argv specs to a raw command; :136 currently prefixes only when tmpDir is defined. The marker must ride the shell command, not merely a spawn env overlay, because srt replaces the child's environment. Define SANDBOXED_ENV = "NAX_SANDBOXED" in this module and prefix every wrapped command with export NAX_SANDBOXED=1; or the combined export NAX_SANDBOXED=1 TMPDIR='<t>' TMP='<t>' TEMP='<t>'; preserving quote escaping, whitespace and ordering. Keep policy checks, shadow input, raw logical argv and LaunchResult.executed unchanged (:112 and :168). outOfScope: Detecting a sandbox nax does not own (a Claude Code srt session, a container): `NAX_SANDBOXED` marks only commands nax's own launcher wraps.

The failure behaviour this spec leaves unchanged needs no new test: a `loadPackageOverride` error for a touched package still propagates to the caller, and an unwrapped run still inherits the parent environment as-is.
`NAX_SANDBOXED` is advisory, not a security boundary: any command can export it itself, and its only effect is that sandbox-dependent tests skip.
Marking unwrapped runs: when the session sandbox is disabled or unavailable the command is not sandboxed and carries no marker.
`nax sandbox exec` (the ACP shell-sandbox runner) and ACP agents' shell commands are not changed by this spec.

No test that calls `skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())` is rewritten, stubbed or weakened to make it pass inside a sandbox.
